title: First Spectral Analysis of a Solar Plasma Eruption Using ALMA
question: Can the logarithmic millimetre continuum gradient across ALMA Band 3 sub-bands be used to estimate optical thickness (and hence temperature/emission measure) of a solar plasmoid and an X-ray bright point enhancement?

evidence.quote: free-free Gaunt factor interpolated from the table of numerically calculated values given by (cite: 2014MNRAS.444..420V)

what.value: Quiet-Sun model C7 atmosphere for background spectrum gradient

evidence.quote: we have adopted the quiet-Sun model C7 from (cite: 2008ApJS..175..229A) to give an example continuum spectrum for Band 3

what.value: Typical Band 3 quiet Sun background brightness temperature 7300±100 K
Flux scale accuracy of 5% for Band 3

evidence.quote: This accuracy limit is said to increase with frequency and is quoted for ALMA Band 3 to be 5%.

recipe.method: Calibrate with SV reference scripts; synthesise images at 2 s cadence for full band and each of four spectral windows
Mean Tb in two boxes per time step; enhancement = enhanced minus background phase (N=29 steps each); noise from XX-YY, plus 5% flux-scale error
Bayesian linear regression of log E vs log nu with emcee

recipe.goal: Derive optical thickness and plasma parameters
recipe.method: Intersect gradient confidence interval with diagnostic curve using alpha (1.04–1.09) and beta bounds; then derive T, EM, density
assumptions: Isothermal plasma; C7 model background; purely hydrogen plasma; background Tb 7300±100 K

evidence.loc: 4.2 Box 2: Moving enhancement from plasmoid ejection

the spectral gradient ranges between -1.6 and -0.4
